account: Today I kept my morning market walk and returned to the office for town accounts. Several residents reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery, which seems ordinary; most others had no news. I have not witnessed any clandestine activity. The unusual detail is my recurring fifteen hundred tea appointment at an unnamed neighbour's dockside cottage. My appointment book lists it for today and tomorrow, yet the secretary says dockside workers could not identify the host and has not supplied an original invitation or source. I remember no named invitation. This might simply be an incomplete appointment entry, but its purpose and host remain unknown. Separately, the builder visited carrying a lantern and requested a great hall lighting inspection tomorrow at eighteen hundred. He says newly installed lanterns need a routine review of their coverage, not repairs. I agreed, and the secretary says the appointment is recorded in a secured addendum. Nothing I have seen proves the inspection and unidentified tea are connected, or that either conceals another purpose.
